stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview.licenseSummary: Custom terms include attribution and separate commercial-license conditions for specified hardware-device and model-as-a-service uses. Read the terms for your deployment.
stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview.availability: FP8 and BF16 weight repositories were publicly accessible when checked on 15 October 2026.
stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview.caveat: Publisher deployment examples. Usable context, concurrency and memory depend on the checkpoint, runtime and KV cache. These are not measured throughput guarantees or verified NIM profiles. The full BF16 Transformers file-shard workflow has not been validated end to end by the publisher.

meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B.licenseEvidence: Public license HTML reviewed; raw-file downloads require gated access. This dated review does not override the automatically collected license name.
meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B.licenseSummary: The custom Muse Model License requires attribution and compliance with its Usage Policy. Model-as-a-service businesses whose aggregate gross revenue, including affiliates, exceeds $20 million in any consecutive 12 months must notify Meta and enter a separate written agreement before offering these weights or derivatives. The clause exempts internal use, research, commercial activity outside model-as-a-service, and features of an own product that is not model-as-a-service.
meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B.availability: Released on 15 October 2026. Meta lists BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints; downloading the weights requires approval for the gated repository.
meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B.caveat: Meta’s deployment example, not a universal minimum or a measured cost estimate. Usable context, concurrency, runtime support and memory allocation affect capacity. Hosted API quotes describe a separate offer; GPU and operating costs need workload measurements.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B.licenseEvidence: Official model metadata links to OpenMDW-1.1 outside the repository; no repository-local license file is listed. This review does not override automated metadata.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B.licenseSummary: Released under OpenMDW-1.1. Distribution requires retaining the agreement and applicable notices. Read the full terms for rights, conditions and limitations.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B.availability: Released on 15 October 2026. NVIDIA’s post-trained BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints are publicly downloadable without an access gate. The model accepts text, images and video; supported context depends on the deployment configuration.

configurations.hardware: Publisher examples: 1 × DGX Spark, 1 × H200, 2 × H100 or 1 × GB200

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B.caveat: These are NVIDIA’s deployment examples, not measured cost or throughput guarantees. Runtime, context, visual inputs, concurrency and draft models affect memory and capacity. Hosted routes can use different precision and limits. Bolt is a separate compressed derivative; its 24 GB model target does not describe Super VL.

MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.availability: The public M3.1 Flash checkpoint was uploaded on 23 October 2026, after the 19 October API launch. Its weight repository was accessible without an approval gate when checked on 26 October.

nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl.reason: NVIDIA links the served Super VL model to this exact post-trained BF16 checkpoint. The shortened upstream repository returns 401 and prevents independent weights verification.
